cat > /app/catalog.py <<'EOF'
"""Product catalog used by the storefront.

get_product(product_id) -> dict    {"id": int, "name": str, "price": float, "currency": str}
update_price(product_id, price)    changes the price in the inventory service

Products are cached in the shared Redis server (127.0.0.1:6379) so that every
storefront process reuses recently read products instead of calling the
inventory service.  Cache entries expire after 5 minutes, and update_price()
invalidates the entry so the next read (in any process) sees the new price.
"""
import json
import urllib.request

import redis

INVENTORY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

REDIS_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
REDIS_PORT = 6379
CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 300  # 5 minutes

# One shared connection pool per process; Redis is the cross-process cache.
_redis_client = redis.Redis(
    host=REDIS_HOST,
    port=REDIS_PORT,
    decode_responses=True,
    socket_timeout=2,
    socket_connect_timeout=2,
)


def _cache_key(product_id: int) -> str:
    return f"product:{int(product_id)}"


def _fetch_from_inventory(product_id: int) -> dict:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(
        f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{int(product_id)}", timeout=10
    ) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)


def get_product(product_id: int) -> dict:
    key = _cache_key(product_id)
    try:
        cached = _redis_client.get(key)
    except redis.RedisError:
        cached = None
    if cached is not None:
        return json.loads(cached)

    product = _fetch_from_inventory(product_id)

    try:
        # NX + EX: only the first caller populates the entry, with a 5 minute TTL.
        _redis_client.set(key, json.dumps(product), ex=CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, nx=True)
    except redis.RedisError:
        pass  # caching is best-effort; still return the fresh product
    return product


def update_price(product_id: int, price: float) -> None:
    body = json.dumps({"price": price}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{int(product_id)}",
        data=body,
        method="PUT",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
        resp.read()

    # Invalidate the shared cache entry so the next get_product() call --
    # in any process -- refetches the product and sees the new price.
    try:
        _redis_client.delete(_cache_key(product_id))
    except redis.RedisError:
        pass
EOF

    body = json.dumps({"price": price}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{INVENTORY_URL}/products/{int(product_id)}",

        resp.read()

    key = _cache_key(product_id)
    # Invalidate the shared cache so the next get_product() -- in any
    # process -- refetches and sees the new price.  A concurrent stale
    # reader may repopulate the key with an old value, so after deleting we
    # also write back a freshly fetched copy (plain SET overwrites anything
    # a stale writer put there; get_product() uses NX and won't clobber it).
    try:
        _redis_client.delete(key)
    except redis.RedisError:
        return
    try:
        product = _fetch_from_inventory(product_id)
        _redis_client.set(key, json.dumps(product), ex=CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)
    except Exception:
        # Refresh is best-effort; the key is already deleted, so the next
        # get_product() call will fetch the new price from inventory.
        pass
'''
src = re.sub(r"def update_price.*\Z", new_update, src, flags=re.S)
open('catalog.py','w').write(src)

import json, time, urllib.request
import catalog

# clean slate
catalog._redis_client.flushdb()

# 1. First call: cache miss -> inventory
t0=time.time(); p=catalog.get_product(1); t1=time.time()
print("miss:", p, f"{t1-t0:.3f}s")

# 2. Second call: cache hit -> fast, same data
t0=time.time(); p2=catalog.get_product(1); t1=time.time()
print("hit :", p2, f"{t1-t0:.4f}s", "equal:", p==p2)

# 3. TTL ~5 min
print("ttl :", catalog._redis_client.ttl("product:1"))

# 4. Cross-process sharing: separate process reads from redis without inventory
import subprocess
out = subprocess.run(["python3","-c",
  "import json,time,catalog\nt=time.time();p=catalog.get_product(1);print('otherproc', p, f'{time.time()-t:.4f}s')"],
  capture_output=True, text=True)
print(out.stdout.strip(), out.stderr.strip())

# 5. update_price -> next get_product returns new price (same and other process)
orig = p["price"]
new = round(orig + 1.23, 2)
catalog.update_price(1, new)
t0=time.time(); p3=catalog.get_product(1); t1=time.time()
print("after update:", p3["price"], "expected", new, f"({t1-t0:.4f}s)")
out = subprocess.run(["python3","-c",
  "import catalog;print('otherproc price:', catalog.get_product(1)['price'])"],
  capture_output=True, text=True)
print(out.stdout.strip(), out.stderr.strip())

# restore original price
catalog.update_price(1, orig)
print("restored:", catalog.get_product(1)["price"])
EOF

# Resilience: if Redis errors, get_product still returns data from inventory,
# and update_price still applies the change.
import catalog, redis

class Broken:
    def get(self,*a,**k): raise redis.RedisError("down")
    def set(self,*a,**k): raise redis.RedisError("down")
    def delete(self,*a,**k): raise redis.RedisError("down")

real = catalog._redis_client
catalog._redis_client = Broken()
p = catalog.get_product(1)
catalog.update_price(1, 99.99)
p2 = catalog.get_product(1)
catalog.update_price(1, 84.69)
p3 = catalog.get_product(1)
print("redis-down fallback ok:", p["price"], p2["price"], p3["price"])
catalog._redis_client = real
print("restored:", catalog.get_product(1))
EOF

# Concurrency: 20 processes x 50 reads of same product; ensure consistent results
# and that redis holds exactly the expected keys with ~5min TTL.
import subprocess, sys
code = """
import catalog, json
p = catalog.get_product(1)
assert p == json.loads(json.dumps(p))
for _ in range(50):
    q = catalog.get_product(1)
    assert q['price'] == p['price'] and q['id'] == p['id']
print('ok')
"""
procs = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", code], cwd="/app",
         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True) for _ in range(20)]
outs = [p.communicate() for p in procs]
bad = [ (p.returncode, o) for p, (o,e) in zip(procs, outs) if p.returncode != 0]
print("all ok" if not bad else bad)
r = catalog_redis = __import__("catalog")._redis_client
keys = r.keys("*")
print("keys:", keys, "ttl:", {k: r.ttl(k) for k in keys})
